title: HELIX Govern: Lakehouse RBAC Model
description: Maps HELIX governance roles to database roles, table/column grants, and row-level security policies across Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers. Implements the principle of least privilege with deny-by-default semantics. Includes platform-specific implementation guides for Snowflake, Databricks Unity Catalog, AWS Lake Formation, Redshift, and BigQuery.

principles.name: Deny by default
principles.description: No access unless explicitly granted. Every new user, role, and service account starts with zero permissions. Access is additive only.

principles.name: Least privilege
principles.description: Grant only what is needed for the role's function. A data engineer who builds silver models does not need gold read access. An analyst who reads gold aggregates does not need silver access.

principles.name: Classification-driven grants
principles.description: Access grants derive from the data classification tier (public, internal, confidential, restricted), not from ad-hoc requests. A role's maximum classification tier determines what it can access.

principles.name: Separation of duties
principles.description: Data engineers can transform but not read restricted PII in cleartext. Analysts can read aggregates but not modify silver models. Admins manage grants but do not hold data read access. No single role has end-to-end unrestricted access.

principles.name: Audit everything
principles.description: Every grant, revocation, role change, and data access is logged. Restricted-tier access logs include full query text. Logs retained for 7+ years (GLBA alignment).

principles.name: Identity propagation
principles.description: Database connections carry the end user's identity, not a shared service account. Agents, APIs, and BI tools must propagate the authenticated user's role to the database layer.

database_roles.purpose: Ingest raw data into bronze landing zones. Write-only to bronze; no read access to any layer.
database_roles.classification_note: Loaders handle all classification tiers in transit (raw source data includes everything) but cannot query bronze tables after loading.
database_roles.authentication: Service account with MFA on interactive sessions. API keys for automated pipelines with IP allowlisting.

database_roles.purpose: Transform bronze → silver. Read bronze, write silver. Access to PII for identity resolution, but restricted columns are masked except through tokenization views.

restricted_access.mechanism: Restricted columns (SSN, bank_account, routing_number, SAI/EFC, tax data) are accessible only through tokenization views that emit SHA-256 tokens. The silver engineer uses tokens for identity resolution (deterministic matching) but never sees cleartext values.
restricted_access.exception_process: If cleartext access is required for a specific data quality investigation, the CDO must approve a time-bounded exception with enhanced audit logging. The exception is logged in the grant lifecycle audit trail.

database_roles.authentication: Named individual accounts. MFA required. SSH key or certificate for automated pipeline execution.

database_roles.purpose: Build gold-layer models (dimensions, facts, reports, semantic views). Read silver, write gold. No restricted column access.

restricted_access.mechanism: Gold models that need restricted-origin data must consume pre-aggregated or tokenized silver views. Gold engineers never see raw restricted values. If a gold model needs to reference SAI for a financial aid aggregate, it reads from a silver view that exposes only the aggregate, not individual values.

database_roles.purpose: Query gold tables for institutional reporting and analytics. Read-only on gold. Sees only public and internal classified data. Student data visible only as aggregates with FERPA suppression applied.
database_roles.suppression: All aggregate views enforce FERPA small-cell suppression (see ferpa-suppression-policy.json). Cells with fewer than the configured threshold are replaced with suppression markers.
database_roles.authentication: Institutional SSO. MFA recommended for remote access.

database_roles.purpose: Query gold tables with confidential student data at the individual record level. Requires documented FERPA legitimate educational interest under 99.31(a)(1).
database_roles.ferpa_basis: 34 CFR 99.31(a)(1) — school officials with legitimate educational interest
database_roles.row_level_security: Functional scope: advisors see advisees, department chairs see their majors, deans see their college. Scope defined by RLS policy joining the user's identity to their functional assignment.
database_roles.access_documentation: Each user must have a documented legitimate educational interest on file, reviewed annually by their Data Steward.

database_roles.purpose: Query gold tables containing restricted data (GLBA financial data, HR compensation/benefits/payroll). Named-individual authorization only.
database_roles.ferpa_basis: 34 CFR 99.31(a)(1) + GLBA Safeguards Rule authorization (for financial data) or HR authorization (for employment data)

restricted_subtypes.scope: GLBA-covered financial aid data: SAI/EFC and ISIR values on AidApplication, need analysis on AidPackage, verification detail, individual disbursement, loan, and R2T4 amounts, SAP appeal narratives, and student employment pay
Restricted HR data (compensation, benefits, payroll, performance reviews)

database_roles.authentication: Institutional SSO with phishing-resistant MFA (hardware token / FIDO2). Named-individual grant only — no group membership.
database_roles.audit: All queries logged with full SQL text. Real-time alerting on anomalous access patterns.

database_roles.purpose: Review data quality, validate definitions, approve quality rules, investigate data issues. Read silver + gold for their assigned domain only.
database_roles.domain_scoping_mechanism: Each steward is assigned one or more domains from govern/domain-taxonomy.json. Their database role is parameterized by domain: helix_steward_enrollment, helix_steward_hr, helix_steward_finance, etc. Each variant grants access only to tables/views in their domain.

restricted_access.mechanism: Stewards do not see restricted columns in cleartext. For data quality investigations on restricted data, the CDO must co-authorize and the investigation is logged.

typical_assignments: Director of Financial Aid (financial aid domain)
Director of Institutional Research (cross-domain, approved by CDO)

database_roles.purpose: Access de-identified research extracts under a 34 CFR 99.31(a)(6) studies agreement. Time-bounded access with destruction verification.
database_roles.ferpa_basis: 34 CFR 99.31(a)(6) — organizations conducting studies for or on behalf of the institution

data_access_constraints.views_available: Research-specific gold views that strip or tokenize all direct identifiers (name, SSN, email, phone, address). Indirect identifiers (race, gender, DOB, major, ZIP) available only in combination limits (no more than 3 quasi-identifiers per query without steward approval).
data_access_constraints.suppression: FERPA small-cell suppression enforced on all aggregate outputs.
data_access_constraints.export_constraints: Exported data must match the de-identification standard specified in the studies agreement. Export logged with agreement ID.

database_roles.grant_expiration: Access expires on the studies agreement end date. Automated revocation with 14-day advance warning.
database_roles.destruction_requirement: Upon expiration, researcher must submit a certificate of destruction. Access is revoked immediately; destruction verification tracked in the grant lifecycle audit trail.
database_roles.authentication: Institutional SSO or federated SSO for external researchers. MFA required.
typical_assignments: External organizations under a studies agreement (NSSE, EAB, consultants)

database_roles.purpose: Grant management, audit review, governance administration. Administrative privileges for managing roles and policies. Does NOT imply read access to institutional data.
admin_grants: MANAGE GRANTS — create, modify, revoke role assignments
CREATE ROLE — provision new database roles
AUDIT LOG ACCESS — read access, query, and export audit logs
MASKING POLICY ADMIN — create and modify column masking policies
ROW ACCESS POLICY ADMIN — create and modify RLS policies
TAG ADMIN — manage classification tags on tables/columns
database_roles.separation_of_duty: The helix_admin role explicitly does NOT include data read grants. A CDO who also needs to read data for governance oversight must hold a separate analyst role (typically helix_analyst_confidential) with appropriate documentation. This prevents a single credential compromise from yielding both admin control and data access.
database_roles.authentication: Named individual. Phishing-resistant MFA. Break-glass access only for emergency scenarios.

column_level_security.description: Column masking policies enforce classification-driven visibility. Each policy defines who sees cleartext, who sees masked/tokenized values, and who sees nothing. Policies are attached to columns, not tables — a single table can have columns at different classification tiers.

masking_policies.description: Masks restricted-tier columns: national IDs, SAI/EFC and other ISIR values, individual aid disbursement, loan, and R2T4 amounts, SEVIS and visa details, compensation, benefits, payroll, and performance ratings.
applies_to_columns: person.identifiers[].value (where type in national_id, ssn_last4, passport, drivers_license)
masking_policies.all_other_roles_see: SHA-256 token (for join-safe masking) or literal 'RESTRICTED'

platform_implementations.snowflake:
CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY helix_mask_restricted
  AS (val STRING)
  RETURNS STRING ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED', 'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED_FINAID', 'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED_HR')
    THEN val
    ELSE SHA2(val, 256)
  END;

-- Apply to column:
ALTER TABLE silver.aid_application
  MODIFY COLUMN sai
  SET MASKING POLICY helix_mask_restricted;
platform_implementations.databricks_unity_catalog:
CREATE FUNCTION helix_mask_restricted(val STRING)
  RETURN CASE
    WHEN IS_MEMBER('helix_analyst_restricted') THEN val
    ELSE SHA2(val, 256)
  END;

-- Apply as column mask:
ALTER TABLE silver.aid_application
  ALTER COLUMN sai
  SET MASK helix_mask_restricted;
platform_implementations.redshift:
-- Redshift uses column-level GRANT (no native masking policies)
-- Create a masking view instead:
CREATE VIEW silver.aid_application_masked AS
SELECT
  helix_id,
  student_ref,
  CASE WHEN pg_has_role(CURRENT_USER, 'helix_analyst_restricted', 'member')
    THEN sai
    ELSE 'RESTRICTED'
  END AS sai,
  -- repeat for each restricted column
  academic_year, aid_application_status, dependency_status
FROM silver.aid_application_raw;
platform_implementations.bigquery:
-- BigQuery uses column-level security with policy tags
-- 1. Create a taxonomy and policy tag in Data Catalog:
--    Taxonomy: helix_classification
--    Policy tag: restricted
-- 2. Apply the tag to restricted columns
-- 3. Grant Fine-Grained Reader on the policy tag to helix_analyst_restricted group
-- All other users see ACCESS DENIED on those columns.
platform_implementations.aws_lake_formation:
-- Lake Formation uses LF-Tags for column-level access
-- 1. Create LF-Tag: classification = [public, internal, confidential, restricted]
-- 2. Tag restricted columns with classification=restricted
-- 3. Grant SELECT on classification=restricted to helix_analyst_restricted
-- 4. All other roles lack the tag grant → column returns NULL

masking_policies.description: Partially masks confidential PII and re-identifying columns: names, contact details, birth dates, alumni and graduate employment details, license numbers, supervisor contacts.

platform_implementations.snowflake:
CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY helix_mask_pii_name
  AS (val STRING)
  RETURNS STRING ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN (
      'HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL',
      'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED',
      'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED_FINAID',
      'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED_HR',
      'HELIX_STEWARD_ENROLLMENT',
      'HELIX_STEWARD_HR',
      'HELIX_STEWARD_FINANCE',
      'HELIX_STEWARD_ADVANCEMENT'
    )
    THEN val
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('HELIX_ANALYST_STANDARD')
    THEN CONCAT(LEFT(val, 1), '***')
    ELSE 'MASKED'
  END;

CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY helix_mask_pii_email
  AS (val STRING)
  RETURNS STRING ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN (
      'HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL',
      'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED',
      'HELIX_STEWARD_ENROLLMENT'
    )
    THEN val
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('HELIX_ANALYST_STANDARD')
    THEN CONCAT('***@', SPLIT_PART(val, '@', 2))
    ELSE 'MASKED'
  END;
platform_implementations.databricks_unity_catalog:
CREATE FUNCTION helix_mask_pii_name(val STRING)
  RETURN CASE
    WHEN IS_MEMBER('helix_analyst_confidential')
      OR IS_MEMBER('helix_analyst_restricted')
      OR IS_MEMBER('helix_steward')
    THEN val
    WHEN IS_MEMBER('helix_analyst_standard')
    THEN CONCAT(LEFT(val, 1), '***')
    ELSE 'MASKED'
  END;

masking_policies.note: Constituent names and contact details come from the linked Person record, so they are masked by the person.* entries above. Advancement stewards need helix_steward_advancement to see cleartext.

masking_policies.description: Masks individual graduate salary so it can support career services without leaking into reports. Added in v0.7.1 for the Outcomes domain.
masking_policies.band_format: Salary rounded down to a 10,000 band (e.g. 55,000 becomes '50,000 to 59,999')
masking_policies.publication_rule: Published outcomes use suppressed aggregates only: median or mean by program with N of at least 5 (govern/ferpa-suppression-policy.json SUPP-001).

platform_implementations.snowflake:
CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY helix_mask_outcomes_salary
  AS (val NUMBER)
  RETURNS NUMBER ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL','HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED','HELIX_STEWARD_ENROLLMENT') THEN val
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('HELIX_RESEARCH') THEN FLOOR(val / 10000) * 10000
    ELSE NULL
  END;

ALTER TABLE silver.employment_outcome
  MODIFY COLUMN salary_amount
  SET MASKING POLICY helix_mask_outcomes_salary;
platform_implementations.databricks_unity_catalog:
CREATE FUNCTION helix_mask_outcomes_salary(val DECIMAL(12,2))
  RETURN CASE
    WHEN IS_MEMBER('helix_analyst_confidential') OR IS_MEMBER('helix_analyst_restricted') OR IS_MEMBER('helix_steward') THEN val
    WHEN IS_MEMBER('helix_research') THEN FLOOR(val / 10000) * 10000
    ELSE NULL
  END;

ALTER TABLE helix_catalog.silver.employment_outcome
  ALTER COLUMN salary_amount SET MASK helix_mask_outcomes_salary;

masking_policies.description: De-identification mask for research views. Replaces all direct identifiers with tokens. Quasi-identifiers (race, gender, age, major) pass through but are subject to suppression.
applies_to_columns: All direct identifier columns in research-facing gold views
masking_policies.research_role_sees: Opaque token (UUID v4 generated per research extract, not linked to institutional IDs)

platform_implementations.snowflake:
-- Research views use a deterministic-within-extract but non-reversible token:
CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY helix_mask_research_id
  AS (val STRING)
  RETURNS STRING ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('HELIX_RESEARCH')
    THEN SHA2(CONCAT(val, CURRENT_SESSION()), 256)
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN (
      'HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL',
      'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED'
    )
    THEN val
    ELSE 'MASKED'
  END;

row_level_security.description: Row-level security (RLS) policies restrict which rows a role can see. RLS is the primary mechanism for functional scoping (advisor sees advisees, dean sees their college) and FERPA directory restriction enforcement.

patterns.name: FERPA directory restriction
patterns.description: Any externally-facing gold view or report automatically excludes students who have an active directory information restriction. This is the most critical RLS pattern — it must be applied universally to any data path that could reach non-school-officials.
patterns.applies_to: All gold views consumed by helix_analyst_standard, helix_research, or any external system/report
patterns.sql_pattern:
CREATE OR REPLACE ROW ACCESS POLICY helix_rls_ferpa_directory
  AS (student_ref_col STRING)
  RETURNS BOOLEAN ->
  CASE
    -- School officials with legitimate interest see all students
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN (
      'HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL',
      'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED',
      'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED_FINAID',
      'HELIX_STEWARD_ENROLLMENT'
    )
    THEN TRUE
    -- External-facing roles: exclude directory-restricted students
    ELSE NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM silver.ferpa_restriction fr
      WHERE fr.student_ref = student_ref_col
        AND fr.is_active = TRUE
        AND fr.restrict_directory = TRUE
    )
  END;
patterns.implementation_note: Apply this policy to every gold table or view that contains student_ref and could be consumed by non-school-official roles.

patterns.name: Advisor functional scope
patterns.description: Academic advisors with helix_analyst_confidential role see only students assigned to them as advisees.
patterns.applies_to: gold.dim_student, gold.fct_enrollment, and related student-facing gold tables
patterns.sql_pattern:
CREATE OR REPLACE ROW ACCESS POLICY helix_rls_advisor_scope
  AS (student_ref_col STRING)
  RETURNS BOOLEAN ->
  CASE
    -- Unscoped roles (registrar, IR director, dean) see all
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN (
      'HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL_UNSCOPED',
      'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED',
      'HELIX_STEWARD_ENROLLMENT'
    )
    THEN TRUE
    -- Scoped advisors see their advisees only
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL'
    THEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM gold.advisor_assignment aa
      WHERE aa.student_ref = student_ref_col
        AND aa.advisor_employee_id = CURRENT_USER()
        AND aa.is_active = TRUE
    )
    ELSE FALSE
  END;

patterns.name: Department/college scope
patterns.description: Department chairs and deans see only students enrolled in programs within their academic unit.
patterns.sql_pattern:
-- Join chain: student → student_program → program → academic_org → chair/dean assignment
CREATE OR REPLACE ROW ACCESS POLICY helix_rls_department_scope
  AS (student_ref_col STRING)
  RETURNS BOOLEAN ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL_UNSCOPED', 'HELIX_ANALYST_RESTRICTED')
    THEN TRUE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HELIX_ANALYST_CONFIDENTIAL'
    THEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM silver.student_program sp
      JOIN silver.program p ON p.helix_id = sp.program_ref
      JOIN silver.academic_org ao ON ao.helix_id = p.academic_org_ref
      JOIN gold.unit_leadership ul ON ul.academic_org_ref = ao.helix_id
      WHERE sp.student_ref = student_ref_col
        AND sp.is_active = TRUE
        AND ul.leader_employee_id = CURRENT_USER()
    )
    ELSE FALSE
  END;

patterns.name: Steward domain scope
patterns.description: Data Stewards see only resources in their assigned domain. Implemented via domain-specific steward roles.
patterns.implementation:
Rather than a single helix_steward role, create domain-specific variants:
  - HELIX_STEWARD_ENROLLMENT → silver/gold enrollment, student, registration tables
  - HELIX_STEWARD_HR → silver/gold HR tables
  - HELIX_STEWARD_FINANCE → silver/gold financial operations tables
  - HELIX_STEWARD_ADVANCEMENT → silver/gold advancement tables
  - HELIX_STEWARD_ACADEMIC → silver/gold academic structure tables
Each variant gets SELECT grants only on their domain's tables.

patterns.name: Research time-bounded access
patterns.description: Research role access expires on the studies agreement end date. Implemented via a time check in the RLS policy.
patterns.sql_pattern:
CREATE OR REPLACE ROW ACCESS POLICY helix_rls_research_timebound
  AS ()
  RETURNS BOOLEAN ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HELIX_RESEARCH'
    THEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM govern.active_research_agreements ara
      WHERE ara.grantee_user = CURRENT_USER()
        AND ara.agreement_end_date >= CURRENT_DATE()
        AND ara.is_active = TRUE
    )
    ELSE TRUE  -- non-research roles not affected
  END;

aws_lake_formation.description: AWS Lake Formation implementation using LF-Tags for tag-based access control.
setup_steps: 3. Tag every table and column in the Glue Data Catalog with both tags
4. Create Lake Formation data permissions mapping roles to tag combinations:
5. Enable column-level filtering: restricted columns tagged 'restricted' are hidden from all but helix_analyst_restricted
6. Enable data filters for FERPA RLS equivalent

redshift.description: Redshift implementation using groups and column-level GRANT.

bigquery.description: BigQuery implementation using IAM, policy tags, and row-level security.
setup_steps: 3. Apply policy tags to columns in BigQuery schema
4. Create IAM groups: helix-analyst-standard@domain, helix-analyst-confidential@domain, etc.
5. Grant 'Fine-Grained Reader' on policy tags to appropriate groups:
- helix-analyst-restricted: Fine-Grained Reader on all tags
-- Standard analysts get filtered view excluding directory-restricted students

grant_lifecycle.description: The full lifecycle of an access grant from request through revocation.

stages.description: Data Consumer submits an access request specifying: the database role requested, specific resources needed, business justification (including FERPA disclosure basis if student data), and requested duration.
Data Steward for the relevant domain reviews and approves (or denies). Cross-domain or restricted requests require additional CDO approval.

approval_matrix.confidential: Data Steward approval + supervisor confirmation of legitimate educational interest
approval_matrix.restricted: Data Steward + CDO + Qualified Individual (GLBA) or CHRO (HR restricted)
approval_matrix.research: Data Steward + CDO + IRB approval documentation + signed studies agreement

stages.description: Data Custodian executes the GRANT statement and documents it in the grant registry.
stages.logging: Grant event recorded with: grantee, role, resources, approval reference, effective date, expiration date, provisioner identity

stages.description: All active grants are reviewed on a regular cadence. Grants without confirmed continued need are revoked.
stages.review_process: Data Steward receives a list of active grants in their domain. For each grant, they confirm: (1) the user still holds the role justifying access, (2) the business need persists, (3) the access level is still appropriate.

stages.description: Access is removed immediately upon any triggering event.
triggers: Employee separation (automated via HR feed — REVOKE within 24 hours of termination date)
Role change (employee transfers to a different functional area — access reviewed within 7 days)
Grant expiration (automated REVOKE on the expiration date)
Steward revocation (steward determines access is no longer appropriate)
Incident response (emergency revocation during a security or compliance investigation)
stages.logging: Revocation event recorded with: grantee, role revoked, trigger reason, revoker identity, effective timestamp
